question: Does the EU warning article say disinformation is illegal in the EU per se, and what DSA duty does it describe for X regarding harmful falsehoods?

answer: No — the article says that, unlike terrorism content, disinformation is not illegal in the EU per se. It notes that the DSA obliges X, as a very large online platform, to mitigate risks attached to harmful falsehoods and to act diligently on reports of illegal content [by_paragraph-dcc3e80f7bab3c578995032535df86d825d4b56abfbbfd449ad738496e887b84].

metadata.title: EU fires urgent warning at Elon Musk’s X over illegal content and disinformation following Hamas attacks
metadata.author: Natasha Lomas

results.text:
EU turns up the heat on X over illegal content in wake of Israel-Hamas war

The European Union is cranking up the heat on Elon Musk-owned X. Late Thursday, the Commission sent the company a formal request for more information — after issuing a public warning Wednesday about reports that illegal content and disinformation targeting the Israel-Hamas war is circulating on the platform, and Twitter’s CEO sending a high-level (non specific) response to that warning.

metadata.title: After warning, the EU opens investigation into X over alleged disinformation
metadata.author: Catherine Shu

results.text: Following the terrorist attacks by Hamas against 🇮🇱, we have indications of X/Twitter being used to disseminate illegal content & disinformation in the EU. Urgent letter to @elonmusk on #DSA obligations ⤵️ pic.twitter.com/avMm1LHq54 — Thierry Breton (@ThierryBreton) October 10, 2023
